rationale: The base station reports uplink_status "no_internet" with error E-503 and "all peripherals unavailable" in the logs, while the binding table still shows some sensors online locally. This matches the customer's report of a street-wide broadband outage after a thunderstorm and the red LED. The base station itself is functioning; it simply has no internet path to the cloud, so the app shows all devices offline.

repair_steps: Ask the customer to confirm whether their broadband is still down (check with neighbour or ISP).
If broadband is down, advise the customer to wait for the ISP to restore service.
Once broadband is restored, power-cycle the router: unplug power for 30 seconds, plug back in, wait 2 minutes.
Then power-cycle the base station: unplug power for 30 seconds, plug back in, wait for LED to turn green.
Check the app to confirm all devices are back online.
If the base station still shows red LED or E-503 after broadband is restored and power-cycling, escalate to FAE.
output.customer_reply: Thanks for your patience. The issue is due to the broadband outage in your area after the thunderstorm. Your base station is working, but it can't reach the internet, so the app shows devices offline. Please wait for your ISP to restore broadband. Once it's back, unplug your router for 30 seconds, then plug it back in and wait 2 minutes. Then unplug the base station for 30 seconds and plug it back in. The LED should turn green and devices should come online. If not, let us know.

results.text: All devices offline, base station LED solid red. Router had been replaced the previous day and the Ethernet cable was in the wrong port. Resolved at frontline.

The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.

complaint: Every camera and sensor has shown offline since this morning, although they were all fine last night. The base station has a red light. I rebooted my phone and reinstalled the app because I thought that was the problem, but nothing changed. We had a thunderstorm last night and my neighbour says the broadband is down on our street too.
